question: What visual feature distinguishes the 'separate intersections' case from the 'single intersection' case in Figure 2A-5?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In Figure 2A-5, the distinguishing visual feature is the interaction of the blue arrows showing the paths of opposing left-turning vehicles. In drawing A ("Separate intersections"), the median is wide enough that the paths of the opposing left turns cross each other within the median area; in drawing B ("Single intersection"), the median is narrower and the opposing left-turn paths curve away from each other and do not cross. Guidance (recommended): - "A divided highway crossing should be signed and marked as separate intersections when both of the following conditions are present: A. The paths of opposing left turns from the divided highway cross each other (see Figure 2A-5), and B. There is adequate storage in the interior approaches for the design vehicles expected to cross the divided highway." - "At the crossing of two divided highways, engineering judgment should be used to determine the number of separate intersections." Standards (mandatory): - Where the crossing functions as two separate intersections, signing consequences follow: "At the crossing of a roadway with a divided highway that functions as two separate intersections, ONE WAY signs shall be placed, visible to each crossroad approach, on the near right and far left corners of each intersection with the directional roadways (see Figure 2B-19)." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-5 shows drawing A labeled "Separate intersections (paths of opposing left-turning vehicles cross)" with a wide median where the two blue left-turn paths intersect each other, and drawing B labeled "Single intersection (paths of opposing left-turning vehicles do not cross)" with a narrow median where the two blue left-turn paths remain separated. - [Image 2] The full-page view of Figure 2A-5 confirms the same distinction, with the legend identifying the blue arrows as the "Path of left-turning vehicle." Citations: - Section 2A.23 Guidance §1 (p.63) - Section 2A.23 Guidance §3 (p.64) - Section 2B.49 Standard §3 (p.114) - Figure 2A-5 (p.64)
gold_answer: In the separate-intersections case, the paths of opposing left-turning vehicles cross; in the single-intersection case, those paths do not cross.
